I have two pages already. Key facts:

- `restart: true` in depends_on introduced in Compose 2.17.0 → available in 2.18.0. Applies to explicit Compose operation restarts, excludes automated restart by container runtime after the container dies. ✓ So explicit `docker compose restart db` propagates; runtime restarts (restart: always) do NOT propagate.
- `required: false` introduced in Compose 2.20.0 → NOT available in 2.18.0. Correct the premise.
- `service_completed_successfully` — need to check version requirement. Not stated as version-gated in the services reference; likely available since 2.x early. Let me check compose file version/compatibility page for `service_completed_successfully` version requirement. Docs may say it's available since Compose 1.29 / v2. Let me check https://docs.docker.com/compose/intro/compose-application-model/ or the "Compose file versions and upgrading" page. Actually there's a page: https://docs.docker.com/compose/compose-file/ ... older. Let's check "https://docs.docker.com/compose/how-tos/lifecycle/" for healthcheck/readiness. Also restart policies doc: https://docs.docker.com/engine/containers/start-containers-automatically/ — restart policies restart container, not dependents.

Also the "depends_on healthcheck" — no readiness propagation for later failures; healthcheck only gates startup. Also note: v2.18.0 doesn't support `required`. Also healthcheck duration fields supported.

Let me fetch the restart policy page and maybe the lifecycle hooks/how-tos to support the migration one-shot service approach. Two more fetches to have at least two distinct official pages — I already have two. But adding restart policy official page strengthens the runtime restart claim. Let's fetch:
1. https://docs.docker.com/engine/containers/start-containers-automatically/ (restart policies)
2. https://docs.docker.com/compose/how-tos/lifecycle/ (lifecycle hooks — but pre_start requires 5.3.0, too new; useful to say not available)

Actually lifecycle page may be about post_start/pre_stop. Keep it. Let's do both.
